entries.core_move: Compute zeros of a rational transfer function by solving its numerator polynomial and interpreting the roots as s-plane locations where $H(s)$ vanishes.
Compute poles of a rational transfer function by finding the zeros of its denominator polynomial and interpreting those s-plane values as the system-mode locations used in pole-zero analysis.
Plot the poles and zeros of a rational transfer function in the complex s-plane by converting numerator and denominator roots into marked locations for transfer-function interpretation.
Infer from each real pole of a transfer function whether the corresponding LTI response mode is a decaying or growing nonoscillatory exponential.
Identify complex-conjugate pole pairs in a transfer function and translate their real and imaginary parts into damping or growth rate and oscillation frequency of the LTI response.
Identify repeated roots of a transfer-function denominator as repeated poles and represent their multiplicity correctly on a pole-zero plot.
Locate poles of a rational transfer function in the s-plane and interpret their real and imaginary coordinates as decay or growth rates and oscillation frequencies for system behavior.
